90407.overview:
Psycastria 2 was developed by Gary Partis and published by Atlantis for the BBC Micro in 1989.

for 1 to 4 players.

You must destroy the ten circular energy pods to be found on each level then land on the main landing strip, signified by leading arrows on the left hand side of the strip. The Psycastrians in their strange shaped space craft will do their best to stop you - and you must take care not to crash into the high buildings dotted throughout the space platforms.

In between levels there is a bonus game in which you destroy aliens which fly across the screen.

90413.overview:
Percy Penguin, written by J.D. Llewellyn,  is a game similar to Pengo. It features two levels of difficulty (normal and fast), each with 3 lives at the beginning. You command a little penguin on a board who has to win against enemies in the form of green balls.

The penguin can push iceblock away to arrange the board or to crush monsters. There are two ways for wining a level: crushing every monster on the current board or collecting the three diamonds. At the end of a level, the time elapsed is used for score calculation. The penguin can be moved in four directions with a joystick or the keypads and the fire button is used to push the blocks.

90456.overview: A game along similar lines to Citadel. Using over a hundred individual screens, this great platform adventure had you once again playing a guy who spends most of his time finding keys, solving puzzles, opening doors, and bribing wizards! This game was tougher than Citadel, with some downright frustrating screens and puzzles. The graphics are similar, but perhaps slightly better than Citadel, with better sprite resolution. The sound, like many of these games, is at best average.

90606.overview:
In the 25th Century, the Earth’s supplies of sulphur had become so badly depleted that mining operations were established on Io, one of the moons of Jupiter. Following a volcanic eruption on lo, the robot-controlled extraction platforms have been engulfed in a burning sea of sulphur and are now malfunctioning.

You have been sent to the platforms in a single-handed, death-defying mission, to collect the precious drums of sulphur, close down operations and return to Earth. To complete your task, you must carefully weave your way through a complex series of pipelines in each of four platforms. But beware of the fast-moving flames and carnivorous plants!

Pipeline is a massive four level arcade-adventure, that combines the best features of a game like Ravenskull, with a novel pipeline system. Once you enter a pipe, there is no going back. You are carried past junctions, around bends and over other pipes to be deposited at the end, wherever that might be.

In addition to an exciting, novel arcade game, Pipeline also includes a character designer and a very powerful level designer. Design your own level, including intricate puzzles and a vast array of pipeline complexes, and test your route through the pipes directly on the level design screen. With practice, you will soon be able to design complicated and highly unusual games.

90613.overview: Perplexity, created by Ian Collinson for the Acorn Electron and BBC Micro and published by Superior Software in 1990, is an isometric pseudo 3D maze game which graphically resembles the 1987 arcade game Pac-Mania (both the maze view and main characters) but while it does share some gameplay elements, the game is a much more calm and organised playing experience with the emphasis on puzzle-solving and as such has been described as a 3D version of Repton.

90781.overview:
Welcome to the adventure! This pack contains a program on disc plus instructions for Philosopher's Quest, an "intelligent" adventure where the player explores a strange land full of weird and unlikely things, some dangerous, some even magical.

In this game the concept of the adventure is exploited to the full, and extended to include abstract thought as a means to progress and survival. However, wild speculation will get you nowhere - you have to use your wits!

The objective is to find all the treasures and bring them back to where you began, but in the meantime you have to sift clues, weigh up risks, spot magic words and remember which way you came. 

Included in this pack is a sealed envelope containing hints and answers for anyone who gets completely stuck. 

This disc features a new Acornsoft dual format design which allows it to be used with either 40 or 80 track disc drives.

91175.overview:
Pengi is a 1-player arcade game for the BBC Micro.

Poor old Pengi is locked up in the freezer again. The player's job is to try to kill the snow-bees that live in the freezer before they kill Pengi. The snow-bees can be destroyed by kicking ice blocks into a snow-bee. They can also be killed by kicking the electric fence that surrounds the freezer to stun any snow-bees that are nearby, and then kicking the stunned snow-bee. The snow-bees can break down ice blocks, and if they touch Pengi, the player loses a life. When all snow-bees in a stage are killed, the player moves to a more challenging stage. Each level has three special diamond ice blocks that the player receives a bonus if they are lined up.

96086.overview:
Predator is a side-scrolling platformer which was originally developed by Activision. It was ported to a range of home computers including the BBC Microcomputer (by Peter Scott).
The game uses the imagery and characters from the movie of the same name. The game is not a faithfully conversion of the movie however - your unit has already been killed off when the game starts and you will battle scorpions, enemy soldiers and dodge obstacles etc, before facing the Predator itself a number of times.
The game is a fairly standard run-jump-shoot platformer, except that you start with no weapons at all and must collect them as the game goes on.

101793.overview:
Plan B was developed and published by Bug Byte for both the BBC Micro and the Acorn Electron in 1986. It was programmed by Andrew Foord with music by Peter Foord.
You control a war drone teleported inside the computer complex and must find and destroy all the computer parts and then escape, while constantly fighting off the security robots. Extra rockets can be picked up and oil cans and spanners will replenish your energy, but be careful not to shoot these before picking them up. Some parts of the scenery can be shot to allow passage, to destroy computer parts or gain access to items, although it may not be immediately obvious which sections can be destroyed. Ten keys need to be found to open the front door in addition to other keys which can be used to gain access to the other areas.

102302.overview:
The Psycastrians have attacked. Using their mind control abilities, they have taken over many world leaders, causing untold war and devastation. Now it is up to you to strike back. Take your fighter across 16 bases, on land, on sea, on the moon, and in space.

Psycastria is a top-down horizontal scrolling shooter. Go across each base, destroy the 10 energy pods that power the Psycastrian war machine while avoiding buildings and engaging alien spacecraft, then go to the next base. Unusually for a shooter, you can turn around at any time to go after any missed targets. Between bases, there is a bonus level that tests your timing at destroying aliens.

102304.overview: Plan B 2 (also known as Plan B Part 2: Mission Unlikely) is a sequel to the first Plan B game. It was developed and published by Bug-Byte Software in 1987. In this one, you continue in much the same way, in charge of a single war drone. Your job is to explore a Togrian Computer Complex, fighting off the security robots. Extra rockets can be picked up and oil cans and spanners will replenish your energy, but be careful not to shoot these before picking them up. Some parts of the scenery can be shot to allow passage, to destroy computer parts or gain access to items, although it may not be immediately obvious which sections can be destroyed. Keys that give access can also be obtained.

124296.overview:
Each level of this abstract puzzler challenges the player to set up a network of pipes to allow an unspecified substance known as 'flooz' to flow through as many of those as possible. The pieces are offered in random order, and there are seven different types - straight lines going horizontally or vertically, corners rotating in each of the four directions, and cross-over pieces which carry the flooz straight across horizontally and vertically. Each of these can be entered from either side. When the flooz hits a gap, or a piece which the previous piece can't flow into, the pipe is finished.

Before the flooz starts flowing from its randomly-selected starting position, the player has several seconds to start placing pieces. They can be put down anywhere. However a situation that can often occur is there will be a long and complex piping arrangement set up, yet a gap somewhere remains to be filled. Players are able to replace a piece with another in the same square (to make it easier to flow the flooz that way), but for a slight scoring penalty.

Bonuses are awarded for looping the flooz through both sides of at least 5 cross-over pieces, or passing the flooz through every square on the screen. Later levels have some squares on the grid blocked off, a few gaps in the side-wall (allowing flooz to thread to the other side of the screen). After every four levels there is a bonus game for points, in which the player can only place the pieces in the lowest open space in each column, similarly to the board game of "Connect 4".

The game can be played using keyboard and/or analogue joystick. In 2 player mode joystick can only be selected by player 1.

124851.overview:
In the final instalment of the Time and Magik trilogy of interactive fiction, the light from the Red Moon is under threat. It was captured and harnessed by the magicians of Baskalos, but its keeper Myglar has turned against them and is using it for himself. He must be defeated before the crystal is exhausted.

The typing interface is typical of Level 9 games of the era. Time saving features include an ALL command can apply TAKE and EXAMINE to every object you can see, and the ability to type future commands while the screen is still scrolling.

18 spells are available, activated using 3-letter codes you will discover while exploring. These range from confusing or angering an enemy to healing yourself and detecting danger.

126241.overview: The second adventure in Scott Adams text adventure series has you moving between London and the treasure islands where you must uncover the clues to fortune. Only by exploring this strange island will you be able to uncover the clues necessary to lead you to your elusive goal - recovering the lost treasures of Long John Silver.

126669.overview: Number 8 in the Scott Adams adventure series. On an Egyptian treasure hunt, you find yourself deep inside a recently discovered pyramid. Find all the treasures and escape alive. This still uses the same simple 2-word parser as the other ones in the series, and is of moderate difficulty.

127701.overview:
The objectives in this arcade style game is to push the cannisters of plutonium behind the safety barrier.
Your first task, however, is to get the Gnomes before they get you. You can do this by crushing them with the Hexoid pods or with the cannisters, though you can stun them by shooting them. With them out of the way you may have to wait for the door to open before you can push them in.
You will have to avoid the walls, all of which are electrified, but don't take too long or the hexoids will start to multiply and make life more difficult - in any case you will need to crush some of the pods in order to get the cannisters where you want them.
Just when you think that you are in control of the situation you will find that the walls containing the nuclids have crumbled away. When this happens the nuclids, which are highly radioactive, and therefore fatal to the touch, are released, the hexoids are destroyed immediately, and the Megapods, also radioactive, appear on the scene. Now is the time for swift cannister pushing, for you are not likely to survive long.

127704.overview:
As one of the four great Gods Apollo, Hermes, Hecate and Aphrodite, choose a team of four mighty warriors to fight for you in the Powerplay tournament to prove who is the greatest. This battle will be fought out not using swords or knives, but with knowledge - gameplay takes the form of a complex quiz on a chess-like board.

You have four playing pieces, which start off arranged as a cross in one corner of the isometrically-viewed board. The squares are split into four different colours, which each represent a particular broad Trivial Pursuit-style subject area. The question has four possible answers, and a correct answer allows you to move your piece one space, perhaps onto one of the four white teleport squares (which randomly places it on one of those four squares).

When a piece lands on the same square as an opposition piece, a challenge ensues, which plays out like a quiz show, with questions asks in quick fire and the first player to answer gaining a point if right and losing one if wrong. The losing piece drops down a skill level.

Once a piece reaches 25 Wisdom Points, it can mutate up a skill level - this makes it harder to beat, but makes the questions it faces harder.

129045.overview:
In Panik! (aka Panik) you must clear each screen of monsters by digging holes to trap them, then hitting them over the head until they fall to the next level. Purple monsters need only to fall one level to be killed, but the red and green monsters need to be knocked through two and three levels respectively.
Points are scored for each monster killed (depending on its colour) and for oxygen remaining at the end of each screen. The top eight scores are kept.

129059.overview: Like space invaders except once the aliens get to the bottom of the screen they take off again.

132410.overview: The object of Paperboy is to deliver papers to your customers while inflicting as much damage as possible to the houses of your non-customers. To make things more difficult, numerous obstacles get in your way including construction workers, rogue tires, skateboarders, dogs and cats, cars, and even the occasional tornado.

132411.overview:
Pole Position is a Formula 1 racing game. Enter the Grand Prix, race against other racing cars to achieve the highest score possible in the shortest amount of time.

Before the player can enter the Grand Prix, the player must first qualify by competing in the Qualifying Lap within 73 seconds or less. If the player however, does not qualify in the Qualifying Lap, the player may continue to race until the Race Timer runs after 90 seconds. The player will score 50 point per 5 meters and additionally 50 points for every racing car passed. When the time runs out - Game Over. The player will have to restart the Qualifying Lap.

Qualifying will enable the player to start in one of the eight available positions. The faster the lap time was, the better the starting position in addition to bonus score points. The number one starting position, is the Pole Position.

During the Grand Prix, the player will compete against the Race Timer as well as against other racing cars. If the player fails to beat the Race Timer in any lap, the player drops out of the race - Game Over. Completing the race by reaching finishing line will grant the player 200 points per each second left on the Race Timer, bonus score for distance covered, and passing bonus points.

135841.overview:
Inspired by the game Gauntlet, Phantom is a top view maze game where the screen scrolls left or right when you move. You are a Professor of Astro-Physics, and with an interest in Psychic Phenomena, you have been sent to investigate four buildings to remove any evil that resides there. You have discovered that each building contains ghosts, monsters and transporters (apparitions that are a gateway to Hell), so with your high powered laser, you must clear four floors of each building.
Touching any of the evil decrease an energy counter and when this reaches zero then it is game over but you can find food to increase it. Use of your laser decreases a gauge but you can find fuel to keep it topped up and there are different types which speed up and make your laser more powerful. As you explore each floor you will find locked doors so keys are needed to open them and there are other items to help you like bombs, radio-immobiliser to stun ghosts and glucose pills to speed up. Once you have cleared a floor then you can use stairs to take you to the next floor.

135842.overview: A flight simulator based around the RAF's commission of the McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II jet interceptor and fighter-bomber.

135916.overview: You are a normal person, finding oneself in the strange world of Piland, a surreal place containing the secret of the wondrous Golden Sundial of Pi. After figuring out how to properly enter Piland, you must find clues to the Sundial's location, with the help (and hindrance) of the Piman, a strange little creature with distinct likes and dislikes. The Sundial is not actually in the game - it was the prize of a contest, won using the clues within the game.

135977.overview:
A Qbert type game in which the objective is to move up and down the Pyramid, painting as you go. Watch out for the Balls or Thin man. Ladders allow you to go to the top but each ladder may only be used once.
Later screens require two coats of paint. There are 15 screens in all.

136002.overview: An adventure game based on John Bunyan's allegory. You play the role of the pilgrim on your quest for the Celestial City.

146738.overview: All fights take place to realistic WBA rules, as you aim to rise the rankings and fight for the title. The crowd frequently shout encouragement and insults, which are displayed using speech bubbles. You need to wait until the referee is not looking in order to perform illegal moves such as kicks and groin punches. Fights last 15 rounds, and a knockout ends that round, not the entire fight. The game was re-released in 1990 by Codemasters under the name Pro Boxing Simulator.

150755.overview:
Defender is a clone of the Williams arcade classic Defender.

You are out in your ship equipped with deadly lasers and a limited number of smart bombs flying over a planetary landscape on a mission to protect the humans that are under attack by the aliens. The player patrols the two-way scrolling landscape in his ship, preventing the marauding aliens from abducting the humans. If the aliens manage to get a human to the top of the screen, it mutates into a super alien hybrid that will come after you, resulting in a fatal collision if not dealt with. Each surviving human gives you a bonus at the end of each stage.

The top portion of the screen is dedicated to a scanner, or radar that shows the location of all enemies and humans on the level. You start out with three lives. Each time you get hit by an enemy projectile you lose a live, once all lives are spent the game is over.

It was later rereleased under the name Planetoid due to legal reasons.

153319.overview:
After the instructions have been displayed, you will be asked for the number of players (between 1 and 6). 
Each player will roll the five dice and then be given the chance to re-roll selected ones. The object is to score as many points as possible in each category. When the score table has been completed you will be given an overall score and, if more than one player was playing, the winner.

153320.overview: A computer version of the card game Pontoon.

153329.overview:
A Space Invaders variant.
Starting with just three lives, you must destroy each wave in turn. A life is lost if you are hit by the enemy fire or if the enemy manage to get past your craft. A bonus life is awarded every 100,000 points. Behind the last wave of enemy craft hides the mothership. This must be destroyed so that you may advance to the next level.

157069.overview: Pedro's flower gardens are under attack from hordes of animals and he must set up barriers to block their routes to his flowers. He will have to take several trips to block off any particular path. Smaller animals can also be stopped by stamping on them. When flowers are eaten, Pedro must replenish them by planting seeds - allowing time for them to grow, as the game is lost if all the seeds are gone. As well as the animals, he must watch out for the Tramp, who tries to steal his seeds.

164339.overview:
Power Boats is a boat racing game for 1 or 2 players. The player who reaches the top first, wins.

Published as a type-in in the December 1984 issue of Elbug magazine.

167571.overview: A higher-or-lower card game combined with general knowledge and survey questions. Based on the UK TV series of the same name.

167834.overview: Freeware/public domain clone of the arcade game Phoenix that was written by Richard Broadhurst and published by Retro Software for the BBC Micro in 2017.

169683.overview:
Painter is a variation of the classic Amidar originally created for the arcades in 1981. Painter's gameplay is very similar to Amidar's bonus stages where the traditional boxes in the screen have points associated with. It can also be compared to Potty Painter in the Jungle which was one of the first Amidar variations for ZX Spectrum and Commodore 64.

Painter's main goal is to fill all the boxes in each frame in a certain period of time by completing the pathways (lines) around them. This must be done before the "Bonus" value reaches zero. To complicate things the "Painter" has to avoid any collision with the "Chasers", some entities present in the game that will try to intercept him and destroy his work. The "Painter" will be forced to restart the phase all over again and one of his lives will be lost in the process.

To defend himself during his gameplay and specially from the incredible speed the "Chasers" might get at the last skill factors of the game, the player has in his power a special tool: a gap creator. This weapon will create a temporary gap in the pathway lines preventing the "Chasers" from colliding with him. It can only be used three times at a time before any temporary gap is removed.

The limit of Painter's skill factor is 6. "Chasers" intelligence and speed will increase proportionally to the skill factor and dramatically at this point of the gaming. Prepare yourself to be ambushed.

179941.overview:
This game is an unofficial port of the Apple II source code to the BBC Master  (requires emulator to be in BBC Master mode) of the classic platform game Prince of Persia, with new graphics and sound.

Game description:

While the Sultan of Persia is fighting a war in a foreign country, his Grand Vizier Jaffar orchestrates a coup d'état. His way to the throne lies through the Sultan's lovely daughter. Jaffar kidnaps her and threatens to kill her if she refuses to marry him. Meanwhile, the man the Princess loves is thrown into the dungeon. He has only one hour to escape from his prison, defeat the guards on his way, and stop Jaffar before the terrible marriage takes place.

Prince of Persia is a 2D platformer that is commonly regarded as a progenitor of the cinematic platform genre. Rather than following the more common jump-and-run mechanics, it focuses on careful advancement through fairly complex levels, emphasizing the protagonist's vulnerability and survival aspect. Rotoscoping technique is used to give more realism to the animation of the characters' movements.

The protagonist must avoid deadly traps, solve some simple jumping and environmental puzzles (such as stepping on pressure plates to raise portcullis), and engage in sword fights with the guards. The player character has an infinite amount of lives, but has to restart at the beginning of a level each time he dies, and must complete the game within an hour. The hero starts with three units of health, which can be replenished with small health potions or permanently increased with large jars.

196721.overview: Planetfall is sci-fi business trading game. The players (game hasn't single player mode) command merchant Starfleet - they can travel between the different planetary systems (with changing business conditions), buy and sell various resources (6 - Uranium, Iron Ore, Machinery, Medical supplies, Computers and Gems), make money and collect them in banks. A game can have a maximum of 15 star-systems.

205791.overview: Plegaron People Eaters are running wild! Trap them by pushing blocks to make a prison for them so they can't escape.

205816.overview:
The objective of the game is to construct the core by collecting all 12 core parts whilst avoiding or shooting aliens. There are springs to bounce on, lifts and extending platforms to stand on and teleporters to transport you from one location to another. There are objects to be picked up along the way such as extra lives, food, laser energy and exploration points.

This game was released only as part of the Peter Scott Trilogy compilation of platform puzzlers.

206185.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Citadel 2 (aka The Fort)
a single player arcade adventure in the style of the original Citadel. It was developed by Simon Storr (Symo) and was first published in this compilation.
E-Type
a single player racing car simulation. It was developed by Gordon Key and was originally released in 1990 by the 4th Dimension.
Holed Out!!
a two 18 hole courses golf simulation for 1 to 4 players. It was developed by Gordon Key and was originally released in 1989 by the 4th Dimension.
Nevryon
an 8 level sideways scrolling space shooter. It was developed by Graeme Richardson and was originally released in 1990 by the 4th Dimension.

206186.overview:
The 17th installment of the Play it Again Sam compilation series includes the following four games:

Master Break:
A snooker style trivia quiz for 1 to 4 players. It was developed by Walter Mansell and was originally released in 1991 by Superior/Acornsoft.

Summer Olympiad:
A sports simulation for 1 to 4 players comprising Hurdles, Fencing, Skeet Shooting, Triple Jump and High Diving. It was developed by Kevin Blake and was originally released in 1988 by Tynesoft with a budget reissue by Micro Value.

Tactic:
A Tetris themed strategy game for 1 or 2 players. It was developed by Andrew Pepperell and was ported from the Eterna version for the Archimedes.

Video's Revenge:
A space shooter. It was developed by Toby Butler and was originally released in 1985 by Budgie/Alligata.

206187.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Hostages
a single player action and strategy game. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1990 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Perplexity
a single player 3D scrolling maze strategy game. It was developed by Ian Collinson and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Pipe Mania (aka Pipemania)
a puzzle game for 1 or 2 players. It was developed by Dave Lawrence and was originally released in 1990 by Empire.
Vertigo
a single player control-the-ball game. It was developed by Ian Grimstead and first published in this compilation.

206188.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Cyborg Warriors
a 1 or 2 player sideways scrolling shooter. It was developed by Tony Oakden and was first published in this compilation.
Last Ninja 2 (aka The Last Ninja 2)
a single player fighting game. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.
The Network
a single player action cum puzzle adventure. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1986 by Top Ten as part of their Peter Scott Trilogy.
Ricochet
a single player arcade adventure featuring Sprat the ball who is bounced about rather than moved in the traditional style. It was developed by Neil Davidson and David Williams and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.

206191.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Ballistix
a 1 or 2 player ball puzzle game. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Predator
a single player scrolling shooter. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Star Port
a single player arcade adventure game with between-level puzzle elements. It was developed by Tony Oakden and was first published in this compilation.
Superior Soccer
a 1 or 2 player football game. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.

206194.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Barbarian II: The Dungeon of Drax
a single player action fighting game. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1989 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Hyperball
a single player Arkanoid/Breakout style game. It was developed by Steve Parkinson and was first published in this compilation.
Pandemonium
a single player arcade adventure. It was developed by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1986 by Top Ten as part of their Peter Scott Trilogy.
Percy Penguin
a single player maze puzzler. It was developed by John Llewellyn and was originally released in 1984 by Superior Software.

206220.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Blagger
a single player platformer. It was written by Ross Goodley and was originally released in 1983 by Alligata.
By Fair Means or Foul (aka Pro Boxing Simulator)
a 1 or 2 player boxing simulation. It was written by Michael & Terry Simpson and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Acornsoft, with a 1990 budget release by Codemasters re-titled Pro Boxing Simulator.
Skirmish (aka Joust)
a 1 or 2 player platformer. It was written by Stuart Cheshire and was originally released in 1986 as Joust by Aardvark and in 1988 as Skirmish by GoDax. It's a clone of the 1982 arcade game Joust.
The Last Ninja
a single player beat-em-up game. It was written by Peter Scott and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Acornsoft.

206221.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior
a 1 or 2 player fighting beat-em-up game. It was written by Peter Scott and Dylan and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Baron
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Angelo Sparacino and was first published in this compilation.
Monsters
a single player platformer. It was written by Tim Dobson and was originally released in 1982 by Acornsoft.
Pipeline
a single player scrolling maze game. It was written by Ian Holmes and William Reeve and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Acornsoft.

206222.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
3D Dotty
a single player 3D take on the PacMan style game. It was written J L Harris and was originally released in 1987 by Blue Ribbon.
Qwak!
a single player platformer. It was written by Jamie Woodhouse and was first published in this compilation.
Repton Thru Time
a single player Boulder Dash type maze game. In essence it's an expanded version of Repton 3 containing 40 extra new screens. It was written by Matthew Atkinson and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Blue Ribbon.
Zalaga
a 1 or 2 player space shooter in the vein of Galaga. It was written by Nick Pelling (aka Orlando) and was originally released in 1983 by Aardvark.

206234.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Camelot (aka Quest 2)
a single player arcade adventure featuring 60 screens. It was written by Tony Oakden and was first published in this compilation
The Life of Repton
a single player scrolling maze game. It was a standalone update of Repton 3 with 40 new screens. It was written by Matthew Atkinson and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Spycat
a single player arcade adventure featuring 100 screens of puzzles and enemies. It was written by Peter Scott and Dylan and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Steve Davis Snooker
a snooker simulation for 1 or 2 players, the 2nd player being either a friend or Steve Davis (the computer). It was developed by CDS and was originally released in 1985 by CDS.

206250.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Around the World in 40 Screens
a single player scrolling maze game using the Repton 3 engine and featuring African, American, Arctic, Ocean and Oriental scenarios. It included screen and character editors. It was written by Matthew Atkinson and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Mr. Wiz
a single player maze game. It was written by John Llewellyn and was originally released in 1984 by Superior.
Quest
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Tony Oakden and was originally released in 1988 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Winter Olympiad 88
a sports simulation for 1 to 4 players featuring biathlon, bobsled, ski jump, slalom and speed skating. It was written by David Croft and was originally released in 1988 by Tynesoft with a budget reissue on the Micro Value label.

206297.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Bone Cruncher
a single player scrolling maze game. It was written by Martyn Howard and Andreas Kremnitz and was originally released in 1987 by Superior.
FireTrack
a single player scrolling space shooter. It was written by Nick Pelling and was originally released in 1987 by Electric Dreams.
Ghouls (aka Ghoulies)
a single player platformer. It was written by David J Hoskins and was originally released in 1983 by Micro Power (Program Power).
Snapper
a single player variant of the classic PacMan game. It was written by Jonathan Griffiths and was originally released in 1982 by Acornsoft.

206299.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Galaforce 2 (aka Galaforce 2: Aliens' Revenge)
a space shooter for 1 or 2 players. It was written by Kevin Edwards and Martin Galway and was first published in this compilation and subsequently released as a standalone in the same year by Superior/Blue Ribbon.
Hopper
a single player Frogger clone. It was written by Neil Raine and was originally released in 1983 by Acornsoft.
Hunchback
a single player scrolling platformer. It was written by John Dyson and was originally released in 1983 by Ocean and Superior.
The Sentinel
a single player strategy game. It was written by Geoff Crammond and was originally released in 1986 by Firebird.

206307.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Cosmic Camouflage (aka Space Blaster)
a single player asteroid shooter. It was written by Daniel Gallagher and was first published in this compilation.
Frak!
a single player platformer. It was written by Nick Pelling and was originally released in 1984 by Aardvark.
Grand Prix Construction Set
a racing car simulation for 1 or 2 players with a built-in track construction utility. It was written by Andrew Bradley and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Acornsoft.
Spellbinder
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Dan and Etan Shirron and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Acornsoft.

206311.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Bug Blaster
a single player Centipede style shooter. It was written by Steve Evans and was originally released in 1983 by Alligata.
Elixir
a single player platformer. It was written by Christopher Hyde, John Llewellyn and Richard Williams and was originally released in 1987 by Superior/Blue Ribbon.
Fortress
a single player adaptation of Zaxxon. It was written by Mat Newman and was originally released in 1983 by Pace.
Imogen
a single player platform adventure. It was written by Michael St. Aubyn and was originally released in 1986 by Micro Power.

206346.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Commando
an action shooter for 1 or 2 players. It was written by Trevor Harwood and John Nixon and was originally released in 1985 by Elite/Encore.
Killer Gorilla
a single player platformer. It was written by Adrian Stephens and was originally released in 1983 by Micro Power.
Killer Gorilla 2 (aka Zany Kong Junior)
a single player platformer. It was written by Christopher Hyde and was originally released in 1984 by Superior Software as Zany Kong Junior.
Palace of Magic
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Martyn Howard and was originally released in 1986 by Micro Power.

206347.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:
Codename: Droid (aka Stryker's Run Part 2)
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Nicholas Chamberlain and Martin Edmondson and was originally released in 1987 by Superior Software.
Crazee Rider
a single player motorcycle racing game. It was written by Kevin Edwards and was originally released in 1987 by Superior Software.
Galaforce
a single player space shooter. It was written by Kevin Edwards and Martin Galway and was originally released in 1986 by Superior Software. It was also released on the Beau Jolly label on both their 10 Computer Hits 4 and Five Star Games 2 compilations.
Repton 3
a single player scrolling maze strategy game. It was written by Matthew Atkinson and was originally released in 1986 by Superior Software.

206349.overview:
A compilation of 4 games:

Citadel
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Michael Jakobsen and was originally released in 1985 by Superior Software.

Ravenskull (aka Castle Ravenskull)
a single player arcade adventure. It was written by Nicholas Chamberlain and Martin Edmondson and was originally released in 1986 by Superior Software.

Stryker's Run
a single player scrolling shooter. It was written by Chris Roberts and P Meller and was originally released in 1986 by Superior Software.

Thrust
a single player scrolling space shooter. It was written by Jeremy Smith and was originally released in 1986 by Superior Software. It was also released on the Beau Jolly label on both their 10 Computer Hits 4 and Five Star Games 2 compilations.

206592.overview: Sid has to walk left and right along planks which are forever scrolling up the screen. Sid can jump off the end of the planks, and he drops down the screen, either onto another plank or to his doom at the bottom of the screen. These planks sometimes have cherries on them which can be walked over to gain extra points. Little white blocks also have extra points in store, but you have to fall through these. A little black monster chases Sid over the planks and, like Sid, the monster can be killed by hitting the top of the screen or the edge.

206647.overview:
You play the role of Paranoid Pete, a Weetabix look-alike space farmer who has travelled to the planet Owwayondah in an effort to grow new crops and send them back to Earth in order to solve the world's chronic food shortage.
The game starts when Pete is beamed onto the planet surface by the USS Harvester. He has to plant the seeds dropped from the Harvester by digging holes in the right places and filling them.
However, the planet is infested with Mega-Wibblies and Pete has to fend them off the plant and himself by banging them over the head with his shovel. Once the plant has successfully grown, an arm extends from the Harvester to take it to the processing plant. Pete is beamed back aboard to ensure everything runs smoothly, but those nasty Wibblies have managed to materialise in the ship and try their best to destroy the Ubik-wheat packs. Pete must use his shovel to protect the cargo.
Once eight boxes have been processed, the whole procedure is repeated with more wheat plants and more Wibblies.

206686.overview: Penguin is a clone of the SEGA arcade game Pengo. It was originally developed with the name Pengo but since it was not licensed from SEGA the name was changed. Some of the inlay still refers to Pengo and also in-game. However, the cover art was changed to Penguin.

206922.overview:
You control a pink mouse whose aim is to knock crockery off the pantry shelves. You have to dodge the flapping birds, bouncing frogs, leaping cats and swooping bats.
The pantry comprises five shelves with gaps through which your rodent may jump up or fall through. However, there are various animals patrolling the pantry of this house and contact with any of them means certain death.

206965.overview: In this variation on an arcade classic, your task is to wield your laser to protect research units on an alien planet from monsters and mine-laying UFOs.

213651.overview: Pinball (called Arcade Pinball on the original 1983 release title screen) , and re-released as Video Pinball by Alternative Software in  1988 is a pinball game for the BBC Micro. The later release by Alternative Software was also released for the Acorn Electron on the same cassette as the BBC version.

216022.overview:
Perseus & Andromeda is Number 9 in the Mysterious Adventures series. As the title implies, this one involves Greek mythology involving the characters Perseus and Andromeda. Hero Perseus must slay Medusa and rescue Princess Andromeda who will then become his bride. To accomplish this, he must arm himself with a sword, shield and sandals.

This game follows the Perseus mythology story closely (as seen in the movie "Clash of the Titans" for example). Many puzzles involve giving an object to someone, who then gives Perseus another object. Entering temples and praying can produce plot-advancing events.

Around this time, the game engine was redone to allow complete sentences instead of the more primitive 2-word Scott Adams parser that had been used previously, although early versions of the game may have still used the cruder parser.

216891.overview:
You are in control of a space ship which is under siege from enemy robot pirates.  Some of these pirates will try and get close to you and then explode, in the hope that the blast will destroy you.  Others will try and steal your 'life-pods', each of which contains a spare ship whcih will be revealed when your old ship is destroyed.

Early Asteroids clone for the BBC.

216942.overview:
You are the commander of a Polaris submarine. 

Your task is to sink 1221000 tons of shipping and avoid your own destruction.

218198.overview: You are in a noisy, smoky saloon bar with six seasoned poker players. One of them, maybe evil-looking, cigar-smoking Black Jake, deals out seven hands of five cards each. From then on you are on your own with $1000 dollars [sic] to lose. First the betting goes around the table until everyone has stopped raising the stake or dropped out of the game. Then you can change up to three of your cards to make a better hand, and the betting continues. When the betting is over the cards are shown and the best hand wins. If everyone else has thrown in their hand the last player wins but won't show you his hand. The next round then starts with another dealer. Moll, the attractive barmaid, serves the drinks and also gives advice if asked! Full instructions and rules of play are provided in the game and the computer will even decide which of your cards to change should you wish to change them. A word of warning: don't assume that the your [sic] fellow players are beginners — they probably bluff and double-bluff far better then [sic] you ever will! Warning — this game can seriously damage your wealth!

218271.overview:
Pharaoh's Tomb is an arcade and puzzle game about exploring a pharaoh's burial site to collect gold and treasures while overcoming timed challenges and logic-based obstacles. The game uses a first-person perspective for movement through the tomb.

Gameplay includes a mix of real-time and turn-based segments. In arcade-style sections, the player controls a cursor to collect treasure items from a screen filled with valuables before time runs out. Puzzle elements involve solving anagrams and attempting four-digit code guesses in a format similar to Mastermind, where feedback is given on digit correctness and placement. Throughout the tomb, the player also encounters monsters that can either be avoided or defeated using weapons, which must be purchased with collected gold.

218272.overview:
It was released by A&F Software as 'Planes' for the BBC Micro, but the cover of the Electron release had the title 'Kamakazi'. The in-game text for the Electron has 'Kamikaze'.

The game is essentially a Galaxian clone, but the enemies are supposed to be enemy WW2 style planes rather than the traditional aliens.

218281.overview:
Polar Perils is a platform game about a character navigating Arctic-themed environments while avoiding hazards such as polar bears and icy waters.

The player guides the character across a series of screens, each presenting challenges like moving ice floes and aggressive wildlife. The objective is to reach the end of each level without falling into the water or being caught by predators. Movement requires precise timing and careful planning to avoid obstacles and progress through the stages.

The game features multiple levels, each increasing in difficulty with more complex patterns of moving platforms and faster enemies. The graphics are simple, with a side-on view of the action, and controls are limited to directional movement and jumping.

419766.overview: An unofficial Monopoly variant, Pass Go (also known as Tycoon) allows up to nine people to play in this computerised version of the property trading board game featuring big chunky graphics.

419927.overview:
Part 2 of the "Saga Of A Spy: The Rick Hanson Trilogy"

In this first sequel to "Rick Hanson" the enemy has made a breakthrough in an advanced weapons system and is thinking of using it. Rick's mission is to discover as much about it as he can, which will require him to get the plans for the system. A submarine drops him at Fisherman's Cove, a secluded spot on the enemy shoreline. The submarine will stay in the area until Rick has finished his mission and will then pick him up.

419962.overview:
Not to be confused with the Superior Software game of the same name.

Pipeline featured on the cassette included with the Micro User magazine, volume 6, issue 1, in March 1988.
The game was also available to download from the BBC teletext service Ceefax in April 1988 and again in September 1988.

419997.overview: This platform game featured on the cassette released with the Micro User 5.04 (June 1987) and was also available to download from the BBC teletext service Ceefax in November/December 1987.

420723.overview:
The object of the game is to position the flashing blocks, which are placed randomly, in a straight line anywhere on the screen. To do this Pengwyn can move in any direction. If his path is barred by ice blocks, he can melt these or move them if there is a space available.
However, whilst Pengwyn is attempting to manoeuvre the flashing blocks into line, the temperature is rising as the 'nasties' melt the ice, behind which they are hiding before setting off in pursuit. Pengwyn's only defence is to outwit them or crush them with a block of ice.

421030.overview:
Pentiles is a strategy game in which you have to fit combinations of 8 different tiles (pentiles) onto a red playing area, with the objective of completely covering the area. Points are awarded depending on the time you take and how many spaces are left in the playing area.
Each pentile can be rotated either four or eight times depending on the shape of the tile, with the exception of the cross shaped tile which is symmetrical.

This is the original 1983 commercially released version of the game. The author later published it in Beebug magazine volume 11, issue 5 in October of 1992.

421323.overview:
You're up to your neck in gambling debts, so when Luigi calls in your marker which stands at forty big ones and you've only got $50 in the whole world then you're in big trouble.
Two-bit hoodlums like you are small potatoes to Luigi's heavies, so it is a very brave (or a very dumb) person who would march into Luigi's and try to place a bet. The only problem is: how to pay the debt? Rob a bank or steal a gem?
What happens next? What will Luigi do? Can the debt be paid? Only you can decide. You become the hero and move around the dangerous shady streets of downtown New Jersey.

The game was licensed from Atari Corp.

421899.overview:
Nine Japanese bomber squadrons with fighter escorts (named raider one to raider nine) are flying by varying routes to several possible targets. As the commander of nine U.S. squadrons your mission is to intercept the enemy before they reach their targets.
You start out with a total of 90 aircraft whilst the enemy have up to 495.
Planes on the ground can be destroyed by bombers; bombed airfields, however, are still usable.

425741.overview:
The Peter Scott Trilogy is a collection of three previously unreleased multiscreen, side-view arcade puzzle games for the BBC Micro.

Network: The object of this game is to construct the Flynche machine by collecting all 20 parts while avoiding or shooting aliens. The player can jump a short distance and fire directly forwards. There are moving platforms, springs, dangerous floors, ladders, elevators, and other dangers to navigate. The game world extends into a large maze over many screens, and teleport machines allow rapid movement. The player has limited health and firepower. They lose a life if health hits 0.

Pandemonium: The object of this game is to collect all 12 pieces of The Core while avoiding or shooting aliens. The player can jump a short distance and fire directly forwards. There are moving platforms, springs, dangerous floors, ladders, elevators, and other dangers to navigate. The game world extends into a large maze over many screens, and teleport machines allow rapid movement. The player has limited health and firepower. They lose a life if health hits 0.

Yoyo: Some hacker with a satellite has caused the player to become trapped inside the computer game they were playing. Yoyo can move left, right, and jump. Yoyo can also temporarily enact a force shield that destroys enemies that contact it. The player has limited energy, but regains this by collecting valves. The goal is to collect every valve over 75 screens. If the player touches an enemy, they lose a life, and starts with six lives.

425859.overview: A 2 player turn based pool game. This version follows the same rules as real pool, except that there are only three balls of each type. The frames can be odd number chosen between 1 and 17.

425945.overview: A text adventure with graphics illustrations where you must travel to unravel the secrets of the diary.

425954.overview:
A two game compilation of card game simulations.
Pyramid is a Patience variant.
Casino is a version of Blackjack or Pontoon. The computer acts as the banker.

438307.overview:
Not to be confused with the Beebug title Power Boats.
Powerboat Race is an overhead view boat racing game for one or two players playing against the computer.

438335.overview:
No. 5 in the Larsoft Adventure series.

Towards the end of the last century, there lived a puppeteer whose puppets were rumoured to actually be tiny people who were under the puppet-man's control.
On the day before the Owlsmore Summer Fete it was discovered that the most important marionette of all had vanished. You are astonished to learn of the puppet's disappearance because during the night you had a dream in which you were visited by Mnemosyne, wife of Zeus and mother of the Muses. She had told you that if you were to help some of her daughters, they in turn would help you find that which has been stolen.

439154.overview:
These two games were the featured ones on the Micro User Christmas cassette of 1984.

Painter (known as Pyramid Painter in-game) is by Rat Soft.
It's a Q*Bert type game where you move around the 3D pyramid, painting the blocks as you go. You can hop into the Tardis to avoid the discs, and Sid the snake who appears on later levels.

Miner (known as Miner Bill in-game) is by Jason Chown.
You explore the secret diamond mine, collecting the diamonds and avoiding the traps. You start in the Down Shaft.

439748.overview:
A compilation of two card games.
- Pontoon (a simplified version of Blackjack) is by M Stein
- Patience is a solitiare game by T.C. Atthow.

439787.overview: As captain of an Elizabethan warship you are tasked with preventing Inca gold from reaching Spain to finance the planned Spanish Armada.

439947.overview: A novel variant of Hangman set to the theme of walking the plank on a pirate ship. Each letter guessed incorrectly moves you further along. Too many incorrect guesses and you will fall into the sea.

450425.overview:
The sudden insistent beep of the search radar alarm breaks the silence in the cockpit of the solar-powered skimmer. As a newcomer to the Planetary Defence Force, you tense to full alertness - this is your first mission.

The recently established colony on the planet Beta Strigidae has been under attack from huge, winged reptiles - the semi-sentient Pteragon. Your task is to destroy the incoming waves of monsters before they reach the settlements. Each member of the PDF must deal with five of the creatures in each attack, and there is intense competition within the force to shoot them down in as short a time as possible.

457119.overview: In this Bookware text adventure, based on one of the chapters of the Science Fiction short story series "The Unorthodox Engineers" by Colin Kapp. You take on the role of the protagonist Lieutenant Fritz van Noon and his band of "Unorthodox Engineers" as Dr. Maxwell Courtney asks you to try and discover the purpose of the indestructible pillar of darkness and its mysterious penumbral shadow, (hence the name "The Pen") which was (obviously?) left by an alien race on this otherwise normal planet. And you also have to solve the riddle of contra-energy. The objective of the story is outlined to the player during the opening stages of the adventure. The book with the short story that comes along with the game helps the player to better understand the story and contains some vital clues to solve some of the adventure's puzzles.

457278.overview: A pinball designer for the BBC Micro that allows the player to either play the supplied demonstration table or create their own.

457967.overview:
Paras is a turn-based strategy game about commanding a squad of paratroopers behind enemy lines. The player leads a team of 15 soldiers through two sequential missions: first, eliminating enemy forces to secure a retreat path; and second, destroying a critical bridge to complete the operation.

The game is played from a top-down perspective and unfolds in discrete turns, each divided into three phases: player movement, player actions (such as firing or deploying explosives), and enemy response. Soldiers can perform various actions, including moving (standing or crawling), shooting, preparing and throwing grenades, or laying and detonating explosives. Weapon effectiveness varies; rifles offer consistent accuracy at range, while grenades and bazookas have area effects but are less reliable due to scatter. Enemy units often remain hidden until they fire, and artillery strikes may occur, requiring troops to go prone to minimize casualties.

457986.overview:
Pro Golf is a sports game about playing golf on two real-world courses: Sunningdale in England and Pebble Beach in the USA.

The game allows 1 to 4 players to participate in single rounds, tournaments, or practice sessions. Players select clubs, adjust shot power and direction, and execute swings using a two-press system with the space bar. Timing affects the shot's outcome, potentially causing slices or hooks. On the green, players must consider slope and ground conditions when putting. The game offers options for wind strength and ground moisture, which influence ball behavior. Backspin can be applied with irons to control the ball's movement after landing.

463113.overview:
The pack contains ten magic tricks and some simple props for you, the conjurer, to use. Ideal as a party piece or simply baffle your friends, here are mind-reading, birthday guessing, card-divining, money-making tricks, and more besides. All designed for the high-tech conjurer of tomorrow's world to challenge the credibility of what is possible and what your audience sees before it.
Let Britain's top showman magician lead you on a spectacular tour of computer magic, and let Britain's top micros take a bow. Together they prove an unbeatable duo.
